content:
alice.dev: Heads-up — planning a migration of our Azure Key Vault usage from legacy access policies to Azure RBAC for data-plane. Want to cover managed identities + cross-tenant service principals implications before we flip the switch.

raj.sre: +1. Main constraints: our Dedicated clusters run in customer VNETs (sometimes different tenant), and some automation still uses service principals registered in our control tenant.

maria.sec: Quick checklist we need: 1) confirm RBAC data-plane is enabled on target vaults, 2) map every access policy to RBAC roles, 3) ensure diagnostic settings send AuditEvent to LA/EFK, 4) rotation + purge protection settings.

hao.platform: For cross-tenant access: you can't directly use a system-assigned managed identity from tenant-A to access a vault in tenant-B. Options: create a service principal/app registration in the vault's tenant and grant it a role, or invite the external app's service principal as a guest in the vault tenant (less ideal).

alice.dev: Does that mean for Redwood Private customers where infra lives in customer tenant, we should provision a user-assigned managed identity in the customer's tenant and assign it to our VM/AKS?

hao.platform: Exactly. User-assigned MI or a customer-managed SP are the usual patterns. For a customer-managed SP we need them to create an app registration + give us a client id/secret/cert, then we do a role assignment in their tenant. For MI, they can assign the MI to the compute and we just reference the MI resource id.

maria.sec: Also flag: if we migrate to RBAC, old access-policy-based credentials will stop working once you remove access policies. Plan: migrate roles, test with a canary app, then delete access policies. Keep a rollback plan.

raj.sre: Practical CLI snippets I used recently:

```
# assign Key Vault crypto user role to a principal
az role assignment create \
  --assignee <principalId-or-spn> \
  --role "Key Vault Crypto User" \
  --scope /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/<vault-name>
```

```
# enable diagnostic logs to LA
az monitor diagnostic-settings create \
  --resource /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/<vault-name> \
  --workspace /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/microsoft.operationalinsights/workspaces/<workspace-name> \
  --logs '[{"category":"AuditEvent","enabled":true}]'
```

raj.sre: And for soft-delete + purge-protection (rotation safety):

```
az keyvault update --name <vault-name> --enable-soft-delete true --enable-purge-protection true
```

alice.dev: Are there any RBAC roles we should prefer over fine-grained Access Policy perms? Seems "Key Vault Crypto User" + "Key Vault Secrets User" are common.

maria.sec: Yes. Use the least privilege: separate crypto vs secret access. Also audit which principals need list/get vs unwrap/verify operations. Keep roles narrow.

hao.platform: One weird gotcha: managed HSM supports only RBAC (access policies are not supported). If any vault is using HSM, you're forced into RBAC paths which influences our migration plan.

raj.sre: Testing plan suggestion:
- create a parallel RBAC role assignment for each current policy principal
- run integration tests against a staging vault with RBAC enforced
- run a canary in production with mirrored access (RBAC + access policy) for 24-48h
- remove access policies after canary success

maria.sec: For rotation: make sure key rotation is automated (Azure Key Vault supports rotation policy for keys). We should record rotation events in AuditEvent and tie to our CMDB so we track which apps use which key ids.

alice.dev: Anyone seen cross-tenant latency or authorization errors when SPs in other tenants try to authenticate? We had a flakey job that started returning 401 from vaults.

hao.platform: Usually 401s are caused by wrong tenant in the token endpoint or expired client credentials. Cross-tenant setups also fail if the SP isn't present in the vault tenant's AAD (guest) or hasn't been granted consent. Look for AAD sign-in logs and KeyVault AuditEvent entries.

infra-bot: deploy: infra/job/kv-rbac-migration pipeline started by alice.dev — id 3421

raj.sre: One more security note: when granting role to a service principal from another tenant, you often need to use the objectId (principalId) not the appId, and the principal must exist in the vault tenant. If you try to assign using an external appId without a corresponding principal, the assignment can succeed but data-plane access will fail.

maria.sec: Action items: 
- alice.dev: build mapping of current access policies -> RBAC role assignments (due EOD Fri)
- hao.platform: draft runbook for onboarding customer-managed MI/SP (include CLI + ARM snippets)
- raj.sre: add diagnostic-settings template and a KQL to surface failed auths to KeyVault

alice.dev: I'll create the canary vault and post the test run results here. Thanks y'all :thumbsup:

raj.sre: Copy that. If we run into tenant boundary weirdness ping me and I'll dig into AAD logs.

maria.sec: I'll loop in compliance for any required audit retention changes.
